h1: Engineering intelligent systems. Building new possibilities.
sub: I build and study software systems across backend engineering, programming languages, symbolic computing, and AI-agent platforms. My focus is explicit specifications, inspectable behavior, and evidence-based engineering—from prototypes through qualification.
w_l: Selected work across programming languages, symbolic computing, agent platforms, research, and full-stack products. Project maturity is stated plainly.
c_l: Omni is an early-stage compiler project. A self-hosted compiler is a roadmap target, not a completed result.
c_1: The normative Edition 1 grammar is the source of truth. Implementation behavior must not be invented when the specification is silent or inconsistent.
c_2: The roadmap separates a minimal Rust core, a broader Rust platform, and a future independently qualified self-hosted compiler. The later stages are targets, not completed milestones.
c_3: Keep grammar, semantics, implementation, tests, and qualification evidence aligned as the language evolves.

a_l: A disciplined, evidence-first approach: understand the system, make constraints explicit, implement in controlled steps, and verify the result before calling it complete.
a_1: Inspect the live repository, specifications, architecture, history, and runtime evidence first. Separate verified facts from assumptions, and identify the actual root cause before editing.
a_2: Turn goals into explicit requirements, invariants, ownership, permissions, interfaces, and acceptance criteria. Resolve contradictions rather than hiding them behind implementation shortcuts.
a_3: Prefer root-cause fixes over cosmetic patches. Keep changes scoped, preserve history, avoid unrelated rewrites, and make each milestone independently reviewable.
contact_intro: For conversations about backend engineering, systems, language tooling, symbolic computing, and agent platforms.
p_helios: Concept and specification for a cognitive-computing architecture with an entirely non-neural symbolic core: deterministic rules, explicit knowledge, managed memory, symbolic reasoning, planning, and controlled actions. Frozen foundation models are quarantined perception-only peripherals; their outputs are provenance-bearing, untrusted observations—not facts or authority. No runtime exists yet.
detail_omni: The repository describes an early-stage compiler. Its independently qualified, self-hosted generation is a roadmap objective, not a current capability.
detail_helios: Helios is currently architecture and specification research. Its intended trusted core is entirely non-neural and symbolic: deterministic logic, explicit knowledge structures, managed memory, symbolic reasoning, planning, and action authorization. Frozen foundation models are isolated perception peripherals only; their outputs carry provenance as untrusted observations and must never be treated as facts, beliefs, or authority. No runtime implementation exists. Specification conflict to resolve: the current Helios README still prohibits all pretrained models and inference services, so the newer perception-only exception has not yet been reconciled in that repository's canonical specification.
detail_aether: The repository describes a specification and host-reference prototype, not an operating-system kernel. The QEMU RISC-V64 product slice has not started.
detail_mosaic: The repository labels the current line a candidate and explicitly reports full-release qualification as blocked. A substantial implementation is not the same as a qualified release.
detail_nexus: The repository identifies version 0.3.0-alpha.5 as an unreleased prerelease. It should be presented as an evolving alpha, not a stable product.
detail_kilo: This is your local fork of upstream Kilo Code. The upstream README still describes the upstream product and does not document the fork-specific specialist-agent, swarm, or NVIDIA NIM work. Those capabilities must be attributed to your experimental fork only, not to upstream Kilo Code; the public repository needs fork-specific evidence and documentation before they can be presented as published functionality.
detail_dnc: The repository describes a governed research/reference platform. Independent production qualification and full tensor-native execution remain future work.
detail_tensor: The repository contains implementation, tests, examples, and benchmarks, but explicitly does not establish release readiness. Performance and quality claims require reproducible configurations.
detail_uep: The repository states that production qualification has not passed. The supported focus is local Windows acceptance; hosted API and OIDC services are not currently qualified.
detail_aios: The repository labels this work a research prototype. The agent and plugin concepts are exploratory, not a bootable operating system.
detail_iot: The repository contains several component areas, but does not establish a deployed end-to-end network, live reward transactions, or production operation.
detail_acts: The repository describes an intended networking product and documents unresolved frontend/submodule layout and integration questions. Production deployment is not verified.
detail_oah: The repository documents incomplete workflows and setup/security work still required. This is presented as a development project, not a production system.
detail_milky: The repository documents reproducible-setup and production-hardening work still required. A public production deployment has not been verified.

a_4: Run type checks, unit and integration tests, browser tests, builds, and relevant security or deployment checks. Exercise failure paths and regressions—not only the happy path.
a_5: Keep documentation and the issue ledger current. Report exactly what changed, what passed, what remains blocked, and what still needs an owner decision. Never equate an agent's success message with proof.
case_omni_intro: Specification-governed language design: implementation follows normative grammar and explicit semantics.
case_omni_1: Treat the Edition 1 grammar and language specification as normative. Record unresolved questions rather than inventing behavior.
case_omni_2: Separate lexing, parsing, semantic validation, IR, code generation, and future self-hosting into testable milestones.
case_omni_3: Use conformance and negative tests, deterministic outputs, and reproducible builds. Component tests do not qualify a whole compiler.
case_helios_intro: A research architecture for a trusted non-neural symbolic core with frozen perception-only models.
case_helios_1: Reasoning, memory, planning, policy, and action authorization remain deterministic and symbolic.
case_helios_2: Frozen models may produce candidate observations with provenance; outputs are never facts, beliefs, instructions, or authority.
case_helios_3: The public Helios README still conflicts with the newer perception-only exception and must be reconciled before implementation claims.
case_nexus_intro: A local-first platform concept for coding, research, analysis, and automation.
case_nexus_1: Give specialist roles bounded responsibilities, explicit inputs and outputs, and a coordinator-owned plan.
case_nexus_2: Tool calls are scoped, permissioned, and observable; a model suggestion is not authorization for an external action.
case_nexus_3: Measure end-to-end reliability and recovery before describing this unreleased alpha as stable.
case_uep_intro: A role-aware education platform where correctness depends on tenant isolation and authorization.
case_uep_1: Separate learner, instructor, administrator, and developer capabilities; enforce permissions in backend services.
case_uep_2: Treat workspace scoping as an invariant and test cross-tenant access across core workflows.
case_uep_3: Verify sign-in, role-specific menus, assessment, attendance, announcements, and sign-out for representative personas.
case_kilo_intro: An experimental personal fork exploring specialist-agent orchestration and NVIDIA NIM routing.
case_kilo_1: Keep fork-specific changes identifiable and do not attribute experimental work to upstream Kilo Code.
case_kilo_2: Architect, implementer, tester, and reviewer roles need explicit scope, artifacts, and acceptance criteria.
case_kilo_3: Require changed-file summaries, test output, review findings, and verifier decisions—not an agent success message.
